PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: Single responsibility improves root cause identification. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if test exercises a single behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert. DECISION RULES: Count distinct Act operations; if only one primary act and assertions relate to it, mark compliant. VERDICT: The method sets up a Grafo, calls grafoTransposto() (the primary act under test) and makes assertions about that result. The insereAresta call serves as setup. There is a single behavior under test and a coherent assertion group, so compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on other tests. RATIONALE: Independence enables reordering/parallel runs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if uses @Before/@After or only local variables. DECISION RULES: If test uses only local variables and no shared mutable state, mark compliant. VERDICT: The test uses only local variables and does not reference or modify shared state within the visible method, so compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should cover happy path and error scenarios. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness by validating exception handling. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if there are at least two tests per method (happy path and error) or explicit exception assertions. DECISION RULES: If class has <2 test methods and no exception assertions, mark non-compliant. VERDICT: There is only one test method in the class and it only asserts the successful path; no assertThrows/@Test(expected) or try/catch exception checks are present, so non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate boundary values. RATIONALE: Boundaries expose off-by-one and range errors. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if test data includes 0, empty, negative or max values. DECISION RULES: If test uses 0 or other boundary-like values, lean compliant. VERDICT: The test uses vertex index 0 in insereAresta(0,0,0), which is a boundary-like input; therefore it exercises a boundary condition and is marked compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helpers for duplication. RATIONALE: Modularity reduces duplication. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if helper methods/constants exist or if tests are short and non-duplicative. DECISION RULES: If tests are short (<10 lines) and don't repeat code, mark compliant. VERDICT: The test is short and self-contained with no visible duplication within the class, so compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and simple. RATIONALE: Lower complexity reduces bugs in tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if method <20 lines and no loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: If method <15 lines and linear, mark compliant. VERDICT: The method is short (well under 15 lines) and contains no loops or branches, so compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple properties to detect faults. RATIONALE: Superficial asserts can miss faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if test verifies multiple properties of the result. DECISION RULES: If test has >=2 meaningful assertions (object identity and vertex count), mark compliant. VERDICT: The test asserts both that the transposed graph is a different instance and that its vertex count equals 100, verifying multiple properties; compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or commented-out tests. RATIONALE: Ignored tests reduce coverage. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test. DECISION RULES: Search for @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out tests. VERDICT: The method is active (@Test) and there are no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out test methods in the visible snippet; compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should map to requirements/tickets. RATIONALE: Traceability helps impact analysis. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if Javadoc or annotations reference requirement IDs. practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests are separate concerns. RATIONALE: Unit tests typically don't include performance/security tests.
